header:
Date: 2026-11-02
Start time: 09:52 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Leah Chen (FathomWare CTO), Marcus D'Souza (FathomWare Head of Security), Priya Raman (FathomWare Platform Eng)
Meeting purpose: Security posture intake to evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment and KMS/SSO/RBAC/audit log requirements
summary: FathomWare is evaluating Redwood for inference powering their customer insights product. Primary gating items are SOC2 Type II coverage, BYOK/AWS KMS integration, Okta SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning, RBAC for separation of duties, and audit log retention/forwarding. Customer is leaning towards Hosted for speed but needs proof points for data residency and key control; Dedicated or Private are options if BYOK and EU-only residency required.
topics: Introductions; Compliance posture (SOC2/ISO); Identity (SAML/SCIM/SSO); Key management (BYOK, HSM, KMS); RBAC and least privilege; Audit logging and retention; Deployment choices (Hosted/Dedicated/Private); Next steps
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Park: hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're gonna cover security posture and hosting options, leah you okay if we run through a quick agenda?
[00:12] Leah Chen: yeah that's great, thanks jordan, we've got about 45 minutes. Marcus and priya are on for the security and infra questions.
[00:23] Samira Khan: quick intro from our side, i'm samira, solutions eng, i'll cover KMS, networking and RBAC details.
[00:35] Marcus D'Souza: hey, main things for us - SOC2 Type II, encryption with BYOK, SSO via okta, audit logs longer than default, and eu data residency in some cases.
[00:50] Jordan Park: perfect, we'll go section by section. first, SOC2 - we are SOC2 Type II compliant, we can share the attestation. we'll also provide our security pack with network diagrams and data flow.
[01:02] Leah Chen: is the SOC2 scope for hosted same as for dedicated/private? any caveats?
[01:10] Samira Khan: good question, the attestation covers our hosted control plane and the managed inference runtime we operate. for Dedicated we have additional controls around customer-dedicated pools and isolation, but the SOC2 report still documents our control environment. for Private (VPC/on-prem) customers, responsibility shifts and we provide the security design and a self-host checklist.
[01:34] Marcus D'Souza: ok, so for private we shouldn't expect you to hand over the attestation as is? like, we run it in our environment and you're not in scope?
[01:43] Samira Khan: right, private is customer-managed runtime, we provide the compliance artifacts and deployment hardened images. typically enterprise customers run an internal audit.
[01:53] Priya Raman: about KMS - we use AWS KMS now and want BYOK with HSM-backed keys. what's supported?
[02:01] Samira Khan: we support BYOK for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we offer an integration path where customers can either use Redwood-managed keys or connect their cloud KMS for envelope encryption; HSM-backed keys via KMS are supported for the envelope keys. small note: in some older docs we say K-V cash instead of KV cache, so i've seen that transcription in past calls, ignore that :)
[02:25] Marcus D'Souza: hahaha okay noted. does that mean you can rotate keys on our schedule? we need rotation every 90 days and strict access logs.
[02:34] Samira Khan: yes, rotation policy can follow your schedule for any customer-managed KMS. we also emit key usage logs; if you're using AWS KMS, CloudTrail will have the events and we can correlate them with our audit logs.
[02:47] Leah Chen: what about split knowledge or HSM where key material never leaves the HSM?
[02:52] Samira Khan: supported for BYOK flows where the keys are HSM-backed in your KMS; Redwood never persists unencrypted key material. for Private we can support FIPS 140-2 validated modules depending on the customer's HSM.
[03:05] Jordan Park: moving to identity, you mentioned Okta — can you confirm SCIM and SAML needs?
[03:12] Leah Chen: yes, we want SAML SSO for user login and SCIM for provisioning, ideally group sync to map to RBAC roles.
[03:20] Samira Khan: we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. role mapping can be done via groups in SAML assertions or SCIM attributes. we also support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows.
[03:34] Marcus D'Souza: audit trail - how long do you retain logs? default vs extended? and can logs be exported to our SIEM?
[03:43] Samira Khan: default retention in the Console is 90 days for detailed traces; we offer extended retention as an add-on (1 year, 3 years) and log forwarding to customers' S3, Splunk or SIEM via syslog/CloudWatch integrations. we also provide immutable export for compliance packages.
[04:04] Leah Chen: does the hosted API ever store input/request payloads longer than necessary? we need strict PII controls and retention policies per workload.
[04:14] Samira Khan: by default we retain request metadata for debugging short-term and model telemetry aggregated. payload retention is configurable by route and dataset. for regulated workloads customers can opt-out of payload retention or route those requests to Dedicated/Private where they control data retention fully.
[04:33] Jordan Park: on residency — some customers need EU-only data residency. what are your options?
[04:39] Samira Khan: Hosted supports region pinning; we have EU regions (eu-west) and can ensure data processing and storage stays in-region for hosted workloads. Dedicated can be provisioned in a EU-only pool and Private gives full control for on-prem or in-VPC EU deployments.
[05:00] Marcus D'Souza: latency and cost tradeoffs then — we run interactive customers, low p95 latency is critical. how does Dedicated compare?
[05:08] Samira Khan: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and better tail latency since you get reserved GPU pools and controlled batch sizing; Hosted is faster for time-to-value but has multi-tenant routing and occasional fallbacks. we can run benchmarks to show p95 improvements.
[05:25] Priya Raman: for the benchmarks, we'll want to reproduce our token distribution and sequence lengths. can you share the benchmarking harness?
[05:33] Samira Khan: yes, we'll share the benchmark harness and a checklist for sample prompts, model versions, and sequence lengths. we'll also run an initial run on our Dedicated pool and share raw traces.
[05:45] Leah Chen: on RBAC - we need separation of duties between platform, analytics, and security teams. do you have customizable roles?
[05:53] Samira Khan: yes, Console supports role-based access controls with built-in roles and custom roles. you can restrict per-route, per-model, and assign read-only vs deploy permissions. we also integrate with SAML groups so provisioning maps cleanly.
[06:10] Marcus D'Souza: any support for time-limited credentials or temporary tokens? we don't want long-lived keys creeping around.
[06:17] Samira Khan: short-lived tokens and scoped API keys are supported; token lifetimes are configurable and we recommend rotating service keys via ephemeral credentials for CI workflows.
[06:30] Jordan Park: Marcus, any legal or procurement gates we should be aware of?
[06:34] Marcus D'Souza: we'll need a standard DPA, data residency addendum, and proof of encryption in transit and at rest. also we'd like SOC2 artifacts and a contact for security questionnaires.
[06:45] Jordan Park: yep we'll provide DPA template, send SOC2 attestation and security pack with network diagrams and data flows. samira will be point for infra.
[06:54] Priya Raman: about audit logs again — can we get a sample log schema? we want to know fields for request id, model id, user id, and keystamp events.
[07:03] Samira Khan: we'll attach a sample schema; typical fields: timestamp, request_id, model, route, user_id, token_count, artifacts, and KMS key_id when encryption events occur. note schema names sometimes change in API versions, we'll enumerate versions in the pack.
[07:25] Leah Chen: are there any known limitations around exporting logs to EU S3 buckets?
[07:31] Samira Khan: we can configure export endpoints to EU S3 or customer buckets. the only caveat is if you use Redwood-managed keys for Hosted, some metadata may transit through our control plane — for strict EU-only, we recommend Dedicated with EU pool or Private.
[07:50] Jordan Park: ok, going to talk through a sample flow — customer sends request -> routing -> model -> response. where are the logs and keys in that flow?
[07:59] Samira Khan: logs are captured at the edge and runtime; KMS envelope encryption happens at the ingress before payload hits persistent storage. KV cache (sorry K V cash) — kv cache entries are encrypted at rest with the same envelope keys.
[08:20] Priya Raman: do you support per-tenant key scoping so each customer has separate keyspace?
[08:25] Samira Khan: yes per-tenant or per-workspace key scoping is supported for Dedicated/Private; in Hosted we provide logical separation with dedicated key identifiers mapped to customer key material when BYOK is used.
[08:40] Marcus D'Souza: re: legal — retention windows need to be configurable per route, and we need automated deletion capabilities for data subject requests.
[08:49] Samira Khan: deletions can be run via the Console or API; we also provide a scrub workflow for model traces and payloads. for legal e-discovery we can provide exports with attestation of deletion.
[09:02] Leah Chen: walk me through how SSO groups map to roles, any examples?
[09:08] Samira Khan: typically we map okta groups -> Redwood roles. example: okta group 'fw-platform-admins' -> role 'platform-admin' with deploy + config rights; 'fw-security' -> read-only audit access. we'll share a recommended mapping.
[09:25] Jordan Park: competitors — have you looked at Anthropic or Cohere? any concerns?
[09:31] Leah Chen: we've run quick pilots with a couple vendors; main gaps were enterprise integrations and telemetry. we need deeper auditability.
[09:40] Jordan Park: understood. final operational note: for Dedicated there's a provisioning lead time and a minimum capacity commitment. we'll include that in the pricing sheet.
[09:51] Priya Raman: what's typical onboarding time for Dedicated?
[09:55] Samira Khan: typically 4-6 weeks from contract to capacity depending on region and hardware queues; Private can be longer if on-prem. Hosted is immediate for early testing.
[10:05] Marcus D'Souza: ok great. can you also confirm incident response and breach notification SLAs?
[10:12] Samira Khan: our incident response playbook is in the security pack. we have 72-hour notification commitments for incidents affecting customer data, and a named security contact for enterprise contracts.
[10:23] Leah Chen: good. last question — do you support attestations for encryption key custodianship and split knowledge?
[10:30] Samira Khan: we can provide documentation on our key handling practices. for split knowledge and advanced HSM workflows, that is typically done in BYOK on customer KMS with HSM modules, and we can help validate during the onboarding.
[10:46] Jordan Park: ok let's recap next steps — i'll send SOC2 and DPA, samira will prepare benchmark checklist and infra deep dive, leah will share okta metadata and questionnaires. any other asks?
[10:58] Leah Chen: also please include sample log schema and the retention add-on pricing.
[11:04] Jordan Park: noted. thanks everyone. we'll target those deliverables this week.
[11:10] Marcus D'Souza: thanks all, bye.
[11:13] (call ends)
